entry.title: Dynamics-preserving graph sparsification. Many dynamical systems unfold on networks of nodes coupled by edge interactions.
entry.summary:
Many dynamical systems unfold on networks of nodes coupled by edge interactions. This work is motivated by the following question: can we remove most edges from a networked dynamical system without significantly altering its behavior? For a given network, our goal is to find a sparser network that approximately preserves the dynamics on the nodes.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #complex-systems #combinatorics

entry.title: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
entry.summary:
We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$. As an application, we prove a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #quantum-computing #logic

entry.title: A Unifying Metatheorem on Weak-Memory Robustness
entry.summary:
Memory models specify the behaviors that concurrent programs may exhibit under compiler and hardware optimizations, which often deviate from Sequential Consistency (SC). Robustness is the property of a program P not exhibiting any weak behaviors when executing under a weak memory model MM, compared to SC. As such, the algorithmic problem of deciding whether $P$ is robust against MM has been studied extensively, and has been repeatedly shown to be in PSPACE for many memory models, such as TSO, PSO, and Release/Acquire.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #logic

entry.title: Python Code Generation for Isabelle/HOL. The Isabelle theorem prover provides an environment for formalising mathematics and reasoning about programs.
entry.summary:
The Isabelle theorem prover provides an environment for formalising mathematics and reasoning about programs. To make verified implementations practically usable, its code generator translates functions expressed in the executable fragment of its logic into conventional programming languages. Its targets have traditionally been functional languages (Standard ML, OCaml, Haskell, and Scala), recently joined by Go.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #logic #software-architecture
